title: AI Staffing Optimizer
tagline: Match labor hours to real demand.
businessOutcomes: Staffing matches demand more closely week to week.
summary: Compares shifts, payroll hours, appointments, sales, and customer traffic to identify overstaffed and understaffed periods.
businessProblem: Managers schedule from habit — same staffing every Tuesday — while actual demand varies, burning labor dollars in slow periods and losing revenue when understaffed during peaks.
outcome: Weekly staffing recommendations: which shifts to add or cut, labor-hour alignment score by daypart, and projected payroll savings or revenue recovery.
expectedOutcomes: Weekly staffing recommendations: which shifts to add or cut, labor-hour alignment score by daypart, and projected payroll savings or revenue recovery.
whoItsFor: Shift-based and appointment businesses with 5+ staff where labor is 25–40% of revenue and scheduling is still manual.
aiInputs: Scheduled hours by daypart for next 2 weeks
Actual sales or appointments by hour/day from prior 8 weeks
Target labor cost % by day of week
aiOutputs: Overstaffed periods with excess labor hours identified
Understaffed peak windows with estimated lost revenue
noCodeTools: 7shifts + Square reports pasted into ChatGPT weekly
Google Sheets labor vs sales tracker + GPT
lowCodeTools: n8n weekly: schedule + POS pull → OpenAI staffing report
Airtable shift planner with GPT suggestions
customBuildStack: Demand curve by hour/day from historical data
Manager notification with actionable shift edits
implementationSteps: Export 8 weeks of sales/appointments by hour
Identify top 3 over and understaffed patterns
Measure labor % improvement and adjust rules
systemBehavior: Advisory only — not wage, hour, or labor law compliance
risks: Cutting staff too aggressively hurts customer experience
Labor law minimums and break rules not modeled
Unexpected events (weather, local event) skew demand patterns
Staff morale impact from frequent schedule changes
